home_cta_description: Follow the getting-started guide, configure your resources, and connect your business.
home_faq_a1: Indie developers and founders building a SaaS with TypeScript, TanStack Start, and Cloudflare Workers. It provides a starting codebase; you still implement your own product logic.
home_faq_a2: The default is Cloudflare D1 (SQLite), with Drizzle for schema definitions and data access. Other databases require you to adapt the integration and migrations.
home_faq_a3: Your own Cloudflare account and Workers, D1, R2, and KV resources, plus auth, Stripe, Resend, or other service credentials for the modules you enable. Setup and environment checks help with configuration.
home_faq_a4: Yes. Pages, messages, configuration, and module implementations live in the source. Adapt or replace them for your product, checking their dependencies and tests.
home_faq_a5: Read the getting-started guide, prepare your development environment and service resources, then configure the project, build your business features, and run the checks. The docs links here walk you through those steps.
home_faq_q3: What do I need to configure?
home_faq_q4: Can I change or replace modules?
home_faq_title: A few things you might want to know.
home_features_auth_description: Start with email and password auth and session management. Google OAuth can be enabled with credentials. Connect your product’s access rules.
home_features_edge_description: Workers runs your app, D1 stores data, R2 handles files, and KV provides a cache foundation. Centralized resource configuration keeps development and deployment clear.
home_features_email_description: Reuse React Email templates and the Resend integration for account-related email. Supply your own sending domain and service credentials.
home_features_i18n_description: Chinese and English, docs, a blog, and a changelog have a structure in place. Adapt copy and content in the source to your brand and readers.
home_features_i18n_title: Content and languages from the start
home_features_payment_description: Start with Stripe Checkout, Customer Portal, and Webhook handling. Configure your products and keys, then define your own entitlement logic.
home_features_storage_description: Native R2 bindings provide a foundation for file uploads, downloads, and deletion. Configure your bucket and connect your product’s file access rules.
home_features_subtitle: Auth, payments, storage, email, and content have a starting point. Configure your services and connect your business.
